en: The Mādhyandinīya Śikṣā,
composed by the great sage Mādhyandina,
states: "A mantra that is deficient in accent or phoneme, being incorrectly employed, does not convey its intended meaning."
That thunderbolt of speech destroys the sacrificer, just as Indra’s enemy [did] due to a lapse in accent;
it undergoes doubling because of the accent when a consonant follows another consonant,
provided that the preceding vowel is not the cause of the consonant's doubling.

"iṣe tvā," "ūrje tvā. If the semivowels (antasthā), sibilants (śaṣasa), and h, preceded by a vowel (svarapūrva), serve as the cause for doubling a following stop (sparśa), there is no doubt that this occurs. (3) For example:
*aśman*. If the semivowels y, r, l, and v, or the sibilants ś, ṣ, and s, are preceded by a stop, and if a consonant (vyañjana) follows immediately before them, it does not undergo doubling. (4)

Free from disease. It is said that a letter beginning with *ka* (a consonant) following a visarga, or one preceding a consonant, undergoes doubling when preceded by a short vowel—provided it stands at the end of a word. Even if they are vowels, they become joined (*śliṣṭa*) only in this way, not otherwise. Examples: *viṣṇoḥ kramaḥ*; *dadhyaṅṅṛṣi*; *aśmannūrjam*. Here, by whatever cause a consonant undergoes doubling, the first [letter] of the second [consonant] and the third of the fourth [consonant] are doubled. Examples: *bāhubbhyām*. When a letter of its own class (*svavarga*), or another, except for the fifth [nasal], follows, as well as in the case of a homogeneous (*savarṇa*) or a twin (*yama*) sound, [doubling occurs].
In the case of the vowel *ṛ*, it is not so in the *śal* [rules] 7; for example:

*tad devānām* (that of the gods), *ṛddhiḥ* (prosperity), *tannaṃ* (that food), *agniḥ* (fire). For the ancestors (*pitṝṇām*), the *k*-class consonants beginning with *kh* are indicated here: *ākhareṣṭhāḥ* (dwelling in the lair) 1, *ākhus te* (the rat is yours) 2, *mayūkhaiḥ* (with rays) 3, *dyāṃ mā lekhīḥ* (do not scratch the sky) 4, *tataḥ khanema* (from there let us dig) 5, *ukhāṃ kṛṇotu* (let him fashion the fire-pan) 6, *ukhāṃ paridadāmi* (I entrust the pan) 7, *khanatv avaṭam* (let him dig the pit) 8, *dadhatū khe* (let them place in the pan) 9, *mitra etān ta ukhām* (O Mitra, these for you, the pan) 10, *tvaṃ khāda* (you eat) 11, *sukhāditān* (well-eaten) 12, *abhārukha* (O non-burner) 13, *gandharvā akhanan* (the Gandharvas dug) 14, *ākhidate* (he pulls out) 15, *prakhidate* (he pulls forth) 16, *viśikhā iva* (like those without crests) 17, *śriyai śikhā* (a crest for prosperity).

18. *bhūbhyākhūn* (Obeisance to the earth-dwelling mice); 19. *ṛtūnāmākhuḥ* (The mouse of the seasons); 20. *khaḍgo vaiśvadevaḥ* (The rhinoceros belongs to the Viśvedevas); 21. [Regarding] the claws; 22. *mokhā bhrājantī* (The shining pot); 23. *ukhāyāḥ sadane sve* (In its own seat, the pot); 24. *madhu śākhaḥ* (Honey-branch); 25. *strīṣakham* (The female-seat); 26. *śaṅkhadhmam* (The conch-blower); 27. *makhasya śiro'si* (You are the head of Makha); 28. *makhāya tvā* (For Makha, you!); 29. Now follows the determination of the missing verses (*galitarcānām nirṇayaḥ*). *īṣe tvā*, *edam aśvastūparaḥ*, *samiddho añjan*, *sahasraśīrṣā puruṣaḥ*, *tadeva*, *svāhā prāṇebhyaśca*—in these chapters there are no missing verses.
1. In the second chapter, thirty-three [verses] beginning with *agne vratapate* have been inserted. 2.
In the third [chapter], "This Agni Purīṣya..."—sixty-two verses have been inserted.
In the fifth, "Agni Vratapāḥ" and "Uru Viṣṇo"—forty-one verses have been inserted.
In the sixth, the first verse beginning with "Revatīramadhvam" has fallen out; from that point until the end of "Paradevasya tvā," twenty-five verses remain.
To Vācaspati, you are consecrated by your own limb; to the Self, O Maghavan, lead us—what has not been lost? Forty-four.
(7) "To the Ādityas you," "Never indeed," "Together with splendor," "The gods who know the way," "Upwards that," "O bath, Nicumpuṇa"—[these] combined make fifty-eight. (8)
In *devasavitar*, there are thirty-nine syllables of *devasyāham*.
In *apo devāḥ*, there are thirty-two syllables of *somasya tviṣiḥ* and *imam devāḥ*, with [the latter] elided.
In *yuñjānaḥ prathamam*, there are seventy-eight syllables combined from *yuñjate devasavitaḥ*, *pṛthivyāḥ sadhasthāt*, and *vasavas tvācchṛndantu*.

In the verse beginning with *dṛśāno rukmaḥ*, there are one hundred and eight [syllables]: *haṃsaḥ śuciṣad*, *akrandad agniḥ*, *dṛśāno rukmaḥ*, *samiddho agniḥ*, *saharayyā*, *punar ūrjā*, *niyāyantam bhavata*.
(12) In the verse beginning with *mayi gṛhṇāmi*, there are fifty-three [syllables]: *agniḥ mūrdhā*, *apām pṛṣṭham*, *mahī dyauḥ*, *viṣṇoḥ karmāṇi*, *citram devānām*. (13)

In "dhruvakṣitiḥ," there are two verses beginning with "śukraśca" and "viśvakarmā tvā"; and in "nabhaśceṣaḥ," there are twenty-five. In "agne jātān," there are two verses beginning with "agnermūrddhā" and "tvāmagne puṣkarād"; and in "bhuvoyajñasyāyam," there are "iha," "ayante," "lokaṃ pṛṇa," "tāṃ asya," "indram," and "viśvānavaitā," which are omitted; and in "parameṣṭhī tvā," there are two verses. When combined, they total fifty-four.

In *namaste* there are two [verses] for Nīlagrīva; with *namo’stu*, they total two, making three; with *triṣaṣṭiḥ*, there are sixteen. In *aśmannūrjam* there are [the verses]: *himasya tvā*, *vācaspatim*, *viśvakarman*, *haviṣā ut*, *tvā indram*, *viśvā*, *naktoṣāsā*, and *agne tvam*; these total seventy-nine. In *vājaśca* there are [the verses]: *vājasya nu*, *devasya tvā*, *yāste*, *yā vaḥ*, *udbudhyasva*, and *yena vahasi*.
In "vinatvam yaviṣṭha," eight [verses] are joined, making sixty-nine (18).
In "svādvīṃ tvā" and "pūtaḥ kuvidaṅga," there are two [sections], making sixty-three (19).

In "kṣatrasya yoniḥ," "samudre te," "uta āpaḥ," "putramiva pitaraḥ," "niṣasāda," "yadi jāgrat," "yadāpaḥ," "yadi diva," "yad grāme," "sumitriyā naḥ," and "yat surāmam," there are nine [sections], making eighty-one (20).
In the section beginning with *imamme*, there are fifty-seven verses entered [into the *Ṛgveda*]: *tattvā*, *śanno vājevāje'vata*, *hotā yakṣadindramṛṣabhasya*, and *sarasvatīmmeṣasya*.
(21) In the section beginning with *tejo'si*, there are twenty-one verses entered: *tatsavitur*, *viśvo devasya*, *pṛthivyai svāhā*, *madhave svāhā*, *vājāya svāhā*, and *āsave svāhā*. (22)
In the verse beginning with *hiraṇyagarbhaḥ*, how many [verses] are there? There is one concerning the Sun alone; how many concerning Dyaus? O Prajāpati, there are not fifty-seven.
(23) In the verse beginning with *śādadbhiḥ*, how many [verses] are there? *Hiraṇyagarbhaḥ* is one; *sam̐yyaḥ* is one; *prāṇataḥ* is one; *agne tvaṃ* is one—there are forty.
(25) In the verse beginning with *agniśca*, how many [verses] are there? *Vaiśvānaro naḥ* is twenty-five. (26)
In *samāstvā*, there are forty-four [syllables] in *ud vayam* (27).
In *hotā yakṣat*, there are fifty-three [syllables] including *devā daivyā hotārā śucim uṣṇihā*; all subsequent [parts] are elided (18).
In *deva savitar*, there are twenty [syllables] in *tat savituḥ* (30).

In the verse beginning with *asyājarāsaḥ*, there are thirty-three [verses], including *yukṣvā hi*, *ayam iha mūrdhā divaḥ*, *ud u tyaṃ*, *viśve adya indravāyū ime*, *yajño devānām*, *gāva upa devyāvat*, and *adhvaryū adabdhebhiḥ*.
In the verse beginning with *savitā sapta-aśītiḥ*, there are fifty-seven [verses], including *yaj jāgrataḥ* and *akṛṣṇena*.
In the verse beginning with *apeta*, there are eighteen [verses], including *aśvatthe vaḥ*, *sumitriyā naḥ*, and *ud vayaṃ agnāyuṣī*.

In the section beginning with *ṛcaṃ vācam*, there are thirteen [verses]: *bhūrbhuvaḥ*, *kayā naḥ*, *kaḥ tvā*, *syonā pṛthivi*, *āpo hi ṣṭhā*, [repeated] three times, *namaste harase*, *sumitriyā naḥ*, *abhīṣuṇo dṛte*, and *dṛṃha* (36).

In the section beginning with *devasya tvā*, there are thirteen [verses]: *devī dyāvāpṛthivī*, *indrasyaujaḥ*, *aśvasya tvā*, *iyatyagre*, *hṛde tvā*, *yuñjate manaḥ*, and *praitu makhasya śiraḥ* (37).
In the section beginning with *dvitīyadevasya tu*, there are twenty-six [verses] including *sumitriyā naḥ*, *udvayam*, *edho'si*, *ehyādityaiḥ*, *rāsnāsi*, and *indrāya tvā*.
(38) In the section beginning with *īśāvāsyam*, there are thirteen [verses] including *andhaṃ tamaḥ*, *anyadevāḥ*, *saṃbhūtiḥ*, and *agne naya*.
(40) Thus, there are one hundred and sixty-four elisions (*lopas*). Together with the one thousand eight hundred and eleven [syllables], [the total is one thousand nine hundred and seventy-five].
The Mādhyandinīya Śikṣā is completed.
